(i) Config drift: ckpts/soup_0204/generation_config.json still carries gemma's do_sample true / top_k 64 / top_p 0.95 (inherited from ingredient 0, exp-02/final), so the checkpoint as it sits on disk would decode by sampling; run_eval.sh's --decode greedy path in package_final.py pops top_k/top_p and writes temperature 0.0, and force-repairs eos_token_id to [1, 106], so the staged copy is greedy and comparable with exp-04's read. Nothing here is null-valued. (ii) fp16 fallback: soup.py's save left "dtype": "float32" in text_config and vision_config while the root says bfloat16 and the shards are bf16 (8.1 G); loading the config with transformers resolves torch_dtype to bfloat16 at the root, which is the field vLLM's auto-dtype reads, so the read will not silently cast a gemma to fp16. (iii) Arithmetic: all 883 tensor keys match across soup / exp-02 / exp-04, sampled slices equal the elementwise mean to bf16 rounding (max 3.8e-6), and 40 scanned tensors are finite. Both ingredients were trained with the identical target format ('ANSWER: <integer>' + <end_of_turn>, loss on completion only) from the identical base snapshot, so the average has no format conflict to blur. Residual risk is behavioural, not mechanical: an interpolated model can lose turn-termination (the card's second falsification clause, >=5 % non-clean stops); exp-04 stops cleanly on 148/150 and one history precedent (r-5720f98a/exp-14) saw a blend produce runaway completions that crashed the evaluator.

Mechanically, uniform averaging keeps only half of exp-04's update while adding half of the weaker exp-02 update, so the modal outcome is a model that sits between its ingredients and near, slightly under, the better one.
